subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Shared Responsibility Model
description: A 60-second lesson on The Shared Responsibility Model.

hook.text: A company's database is exposed to the internet. Whose fault? The cloud provider's or the customer's?

buildup.text: Cloud security is split: the provider secures the infrastructure, the customer secures what runs on it.

discovery.text: AWS calls it 'security of the cloud vs. security in the cloud.' The line varies by service model.

twist.text: Over 90% of cloud security failures are the customer's fault. Misconfiguration is the top cause.

climax.text: Understanding where your responsibility starts is the single most important cloud security concept.

punchline.text: The provider secures the cloud. You secure what's in it.

quiz.question: What causes over 90% of cloud security failures?
options: Customer misconfiguration, not cloud provider vulnerabilities
Cloud providers using outdated encryption methods

details.summary: Cloud security follows a shared responsibility model where the provider secures the infrastructure and the customer secures their data, configurations, and access. Misunderstanding this boundary is behind most cloud breaches.
details.whyItMatters: Many organizations assume the cloud provider handles all security. Clarifying who owns what prevents dangerous gaps in protection.
takeaways: Providers secure hardware, networking, and host OS
Customers secure data, identities, and configurations
Most breaches stem from customer-side misconfigurations

faq.question: What does the cloud provider secure?
faq.answer: The provider secures physical data centers, networking hardware, hypervisors, and the host operating system. They handle patching of the underlying infrastructure and ensuring physical access controls, power, and cooling meet security standards.

faq.question: What is the customer responsible for?
faq.answer: Customers must secure their data, manage identity and access controls, configure firewalls and network rules, encrypt sensitive information, and keep their applications and guest operating systems patched and updated.
